definition: Renewable-energy measures provide renewable electricity for project-financed operations, equipment or facilities. Counts when the project finances, installs, procures or explicitly requires solar, wind or another renewable-energy source, including renewable generation combined with storage. The defining intervention is substitution or provision of electricity from a renewable source rather than continuity during an outage. Renewable systems may additionally count under backup_power when the project explicitly uses them to maintain operations after loss of the primary electricity supply. Does not count for the national electricity mix, unrelated power-sector investments, national renewable-energy targets, generic low-carbon commitments or renewable energy mentioned only as context. Does not count where renewable electricity is itself what the project delivers to households, businesses or communities (energy access, mini-grid, solar home system or electrification programmes); that is a power-sector investment, not a measure for a project-financed asset.
boundary: The project supplies electricity from a renewable source as the normal supply.
note: Renewable_energy is defined by the source of electricity; backup_power is defined by continuity during failure of the primary supply. Do not force a choice between them when both functions are explicitly financed. v4 (2026-10-20): Dev's revision; measures are defined by the intervention, the asset map gives the asset. v5 (2026-10-21): grade 1 adds existing systems, results-framework indicators, economic-analysis assumptions and other World Bank projects; types rewritten to exclude each other and asked as one choice.
